en: He states the extraction of the thorn because there would be a fault in constructing monasteries and so forth on ground that contains a thorn.
Since it would constitute a fault to construct monasteries and the like on ground containing subterranean minerals, the extraction of such minerals from the earth shall now be described.

First of all, the preceptor, having seated a girl possessing the auspicious marks—born of one of the five families, or in their absence, born of another family—upon a soft seat in the center of a ground divided into nine squares, should with a concentrated mind visualize her as the form of the Blessed Lady; having worshipped her diligently, he should examine whatever words she utters in satisfaction, whether they be questions or answers.

First, for the time being, the master [should select] a young girl endowed with the [required] characteristics, whether she be born of a noble family or, if such is unavailable, even from another caste.

Having placed [the manuscript] upon a very soft seat in the center of a nine-fold arrangement of mirrors, one should, with a mind in meditative equipoise, diligently visualize those [letters] in the form of the Blessed One; having made perfect offerings, one should then definitively examine the syllables of the answers given to the questions asked in sequence.
Namely as follows:
That is to say:
when these syllables— va, ka, ca, ta, e, hā, śa, ya, yā—
occur in a question regarding a site divided into nine parts, there is a stake (śalya) located there starting from the east.

*Ba ka tsa ta ae h’a sha ya y’a* | {55a7} Wherever these syllables are inquired about, there one should understand the directions—east and so forth—within the earth divided into nine parts: "If [the letter] *vi* appears in the eastern sector (*aindryām*) when questioned, it indicates a human stake (*mānuṣaśalya*) at a distance of one and a half cubits;
it brings about the death of a person residing in that house, of this there is no doubt."
Regarding what is called "the life of inquiry," at a distance of one and a half cubits from the side of the sense-faculties, there is a human obstacle; humans residing there will certainly die.
In the southeast, according to the *Kaprashna*,
a *kharaśalya* situated at the level of the waist within the house causes incomparable fear of royal punishment and serpents.

When asked, "What is it? he says, "A *ka*. Since there is a donkey's skull at about waist-height on the side of the fire, those staying in that place suffer the king’s punishment, the fear of being trampled, and the loss of their livelihood.
If a *naraśalya* occurs at the level of the waist in the southern direction during an inquiry,
it produces death for the master of the house itself, having entered that very abode.

When asked, "Tsa? at that time, because there is a human settlement (*manuṣya-sela*) at the southern waist [of the world], it causes the death of the householders dwelling in that place with certainty.
If, when questioned regarding the direction of the Rākṣasas, a dog's bone is found at a distance of one and a half cubits,
it will certainly cause the destruction of children in that house before long.

When questioned, it was said: "At a distance of one and a half cubits toward the direction of the rākṣasas, there is bone; therefore, the children of those dwelling in that house will certainly perish."
In this question, if there is a "child-fragment" (śiśuśalya) in the western quarter at a distance of one and a half cubits,
it causes the constant absence of the husband and leaves his house empty.
When asked, he said: "Because there is a half-cubit of the water-lord’s direction and a removal [of obstacles] implied therein, the owner has evicted me and constantly keeps that house empty."
In the northwest, according to the *Hapraśna*, know that there are charcoal-like men four cubits in height;
they cause the manifestation of bad dreams and the destruction of friends.

When questioned, if one says "hā," one should know that there is a stone in the northwest direction at a distance of four cubits; this causes one to see very bad dreams and brings ruin to one's companions.
If the "thorn of the twice-born" (dvijaśalya) occurs in the north during the inquiry of the letter Śa, it is situated at the level of the hips;
it indeed quickly renders even a wealthy householder destitute.

Gloss: "Residing in that house" means that when one sees [the sign] called "meat," because there is a *dvija* (bird) in the middle part of the first portion of the body, those residing in that house will certainly and swiftly be deprived of their wealth, even if they are like Vaiśravaṇa.
In the northeast, according to the *Yapraśna*, there is a cow-pen measuring one and a half cubits;
if it enters a house, it causes the destruction of cattle wealth, without a doubt.

When questioned, if one says "ya," there is a bull-demon (*goḍākinī*) at a distance of one and a half cubits in the southeast; those dwelling in that place will undoubtedly suffer the loss of their cattle and wealth.
Know that there is an internal arrow made of human child-skulls, ashes, and iron;
she who, while residing in the house, brings about the destruction of each individual family.

When asked, [if one says] "ya," it means that because human hair, a skull, ashes, and iron tongs are present in the center, one should know that those who dwell in that house will have their respective lineages destroyed.
Having thus recognized this harmful thorn and having extracted it with effort,
one should then firmly plant a jewel-studded peg upon the purified ground.
Having thus recognized that the pebbles are flawed, one should extract them with great effort and drive in the pegs once again upon that delightful, authentic ground.

A probe made of silver, copper, brass, iron, stone, wood, or bone is not recommended; it lacks the power of the lineage and, being unstable, brings about the destruction of prosperity and bestows disease.
A golden probe, however, bestows the success of strength, welfare, and wealth for the people.
A firm wooden stake, and striking it with a hammer made of copper mixed with honey.

It is not taught that [vessels] made from silver, copper, black tin, white tin, or iron, nor those made from stone, wood, or bone, possess these qualities; for they lack a fixed nature, and their power, stability, and excellence are exhausted, as they bring about disease.
The golden probe bestows progeny, strength, happiness, wealth, and accomplishment. Bṛhaspati [is represented] by a staff made of the grapevine, which is to be struck with iron.
This is the procedure for the extraction of the arrowhead (iti śalyoddharaṇavidhiḥ). 4.
Thus is the ritual for extracting [and] clearing away [impurities].
